readmeExcerpt:
# Pyrite64

N64 game-engine and editor using Libdragon and tiny3d.


    

    

> Note: This project does NOT use any proprietary N64 SDKs or libraries. Pyrite64 is a visual editor + runtime-engine to create 3D games that can run on a real N64 console or accurate emulators.
Besides the usual editor, some extra features include: - Automatic toolchain installation on Windows - 3D-Model import (GLTF) from blender with [fast64](https://github.com/Fast-64/fast64) material support. - Support for HDR+Bloom rendering (shown here: www.youtube.com/watch?v=XP8g2ngHftY) - Support for big-texture rendering (256x256) (shown here: www.youtube.com/watch?v=rNEo0aQkGnU) - Runtime engine handling scene-management, rendering, collision, audio and more. - Global asset management with automatic memory cleanup - Node-Graph editor to script basic control flow Note that this project focuses on real hardware, so accurate emulation is required to run/test games on PC.
Emulators that are accurate enough include [Ares (v147 or newer)](https://ares-emu.net/) and [gopher64](https://github.com/gopher64/gopher64). > [!WARNING] > This project is still in early development, so features are going to be missing.
> Documentation is also still a work in progress, and breaking API changes are to be expected. ## Documentation Before starting, please read the [FAQ](https://hailtododongo.github.io/pyrite64/docs/faq.html)!
General documentation is available here: [Documentation](https://hailtododongo.github.io/pyrite64/)
This also contains information on how to build the editor. The source-code for the docs can be found in this repo under `/docs`. ## Showcase


Cathode Quest 64 (YouTube)    |    Pyrite64 Release Video          

## Links For anything N64 homebrew related,
checkout the N64Brew discord: https://discord.gg/WqFgNWf ## Credits & License © 2025-2026 - Max Bebök (HailToDodongo)
Pyrite64 is licensed under the MIT License, see the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for more information.
Licenses for external libraries used in the editor can be found in their respective directory under `/vendored` Pyrite64 does NOT force any restrictions or licenses on games made with it.
Pyrite64 does NOT claim any copyright or force licenses for assets / source-code generated by the editor. While not required, please consider crediting Pyrite64 with a logo and/or name in your credits and/or boot logo sequence.
readmeHtml:
Pyrite64

N64 game-engine and editor using Libdragon and tiny3d.


    

    

Note: This project does NOT use any proprietary N64 SDKs or libraries.

Pyrite64 is a visual editor + runtime-engine to create 3D games that can run on a real N64 console or accurate emulators.
Besides the usual editor, some extra features include:

  • Automatic toolchain installation on Windows
  • 3D-Model import (GLTF) from blender with fast64 material support.
  • Support for HDR+Bloom rendering (shown here: www.youtube.com/watch?v=XP8g2ngHftY)
  • Support for big-texture rendering (256x256) (shown here: www.youtube.com/watch?v=rNEo0aQkGnU)
  • Runtime engine handling scene-management, rendering, collision, audio and more.
  • Global asset management with automatic memory cleanup
  • Node-Graph editor to script basic control flow

Note that this project focuses on real hardware, so accurate emulation is required to run/test games on PC.
Emulators that are accurate enough include Ares (v147 or newer) and gopher64.

Warning

This project is still in early development, so features are going to be missing.
Documentation is also still a work in progress, and breaking API changes are to be expected.

Documentation

Before starting, please read the FAQ!
General documentation is available here: Documentation
This also contains information on how to build the editor.

The source-code for the docs can be found in this repo under /docs.

Showcase


Cathode Quest 64 (YouTube)    |    Pyrite64 Release Video          

Links

For anything N64 homebrew related,
checkout the N64Brew discord: https://discord.gg/WqFgNWf

Credits & License

© 2025-2026 - Max Bebök (HailToDodongo)

Pyrite64 is licensed under the MIT License, see the LICENSE file for more information.
Licenses for external libraries used in the editor can be found in their respective directory under /vendored

Pyrite64 does NOT force any restrictions or licenses on games made with it.

While not required, please consider crediting Pyrite64 with a logo and/or name in your credits and/or boot logo sequence.

# v0.10.0 - Changelog

## What's Changed

### Editor
* VSCode project generator (on new project + manual) by @HailToDodongo in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/329
* Add template-selection during project creation by @HailToDodongo in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/330
* Fix: Correct lock-Icon size when zoomed by @HailToDodongo in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/331
* Support editor side bool and color picker arguments in code components, add Range & Min/Max attributes by @Byterset in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/336
* fix excessive history with input/color picker by @HailToDodongo in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/338
* Preview Fog in the editor + setting to not do so by @HailToDodongo in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/341
* Texture Picker (preview and search textures) by @KevinLKs in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/342
* Add P64::Group attribute to group arguments by @HailToDodongo in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/348
* fix: broken asset table when toggling exclude setting by @HailToDodongo in https://github.com/HailToDodongo/pyrite64/pull/333

aiSummary.oneLiner: A visual 3D game engine and node-graph editor for creating native Nintendo 64 homebrew games legally.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Pyrite64 is a comprehensive game development environment engineered to create custom 3D games that run natively on real Nintendo 64 hardware or highly accurate emulators. It consists of a sophisticated visual editor and a dedicated runtime engine that leverages the modern, open-source Libdragon SDK and tiny3d library, entirely avoiding proprietary Nintendo SDKs. The project radically simplifies the historically difficult process of N64 homebrew development by providing modern toolchains and automated memory management. It uniquely introduces advanced features like HDR+Bloom rendering, massive-texture support, and a node-graph editor for visual scripting, bringing modern creative workflows directly to late-90s hardware constraints.
keyFeatures: Visual level editor: Provides a robust, modern graphical interface for seamlessly constructing 3D environments and placing game entities.
Native hardware runtime: Accurately compiles games that run directly on original N64 hardware without ever relying on proprietary or illegal SDKs.
Libdragon integration: Built firmly on the modern, open-source Libdragon toolchain to guarantee legal, accessible, and fast homebrew development.
Direct Blender workflow: Directly supports importing standard GLTF 3D models from Blender using the widely adopted fast64 plugin architecture.
Node-graph editor: Allows developers and artists to visually script basic control flow logic without constantly writing low-level C code.

useCases.title: N64 homebrew development
useCases.description: Developers securely and legally compile original 3D games for the Nintendo 64 console using modern graphical tools and automated workflows.

useCases.title: Retro game design
useCases.description: Designers visually construct intricate levels without needing to write complex, low-level C code for spatial positioning and entity management.

useCases.title: 3D asset integration
useCases.description: Artists easily bridge modern 3D modeling workflows in Blender with the incredibly strict memory and hardware constraints of late-90s consoles.

useCases.title: Engine runtime execution
useCases.description: Programmers efficiently manage scene rendering, collision detection, and crucial memory cleanup through a dedicated runtime engine tailored specifically for the N64.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Retro game developers, homebrew enthusiasts, and 3D artists who want to create software for the Nintendo 64 using modern visual tools and legal toolchains.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Read the documentation at https://hailtododongo.github.io/pyrite64/ for toolchain setup instructions.
